    embed-resources: true
    include-in-header:
      text: |
        <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
        <link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Barlow+Condensed:ital,wght@0,400;0,500;0,600;0,700;1,400;1,600&family=Nunito+Sans:ital,opsz,wght@0,6..12,200..1000;1,6..12,200..1000&family=Source+Serif+4:ital,opsz,wght@0,8..60,200..900;1,8..60,200..900&family=Oswald:wght@500;600;700&family=Nunito:ital,wght@0,400;0,600;0,700;0,800;1,400&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">
    include-after-body:
      text: |
        <script>
        // GW brand fonts first, free substitutes second: if Gazzetta is not
        // installed, switch the display weights and scale to Barlow Condensed.
        (function () {
          function detect() {
            var forced = /[?&]fonts=substitutes/.test(location.search);
            var ctx = document.createElement('canvas').getContext('2d');
            var probe = 'mmmmmmmmmmlli';
            ctx.font = '100px monospace';
            var mono = ctx.measureText(probe).width;
            ctx.font = '100px "Gazzetta", monospace';
            var has = ctx.measureText(probe).width !== mono;
            document.documentElement.classList.toggle('gw-substitute-fonts', forced || !has);
          }
          detect();
          if (document.fonts && document.fonts.ready) document.fonts.ready.then(detect);
        })();
        // Embedded talks: load each iframe only when its slide is shown, so a
        // missing connection never slows the rest of the deck. (Created here,
        // not in the markdown, so the render step doesn't inline the page.)
        // Theme switcher: GW and TODO Group logos in each slide header toggle the theme.
        document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () {
          var root = document.documentElement;
          var saved = null;
          try { saved = localStorage.getItem('deck-theme'); } catch (e) {}
          var m = /[?&]theme=(gw|todo)/.exec(location.search);
          var current = m ? m[1] : (saved === 'todo' ? 'todo' : 'gw');
          var sections = document.querySelectorAll('.reveal .slides > section');
          sections.forEach(function (sec) {
            var box = document.createElement('div');
            box.className = 'hdr-logos';
            [['ospo', 'gw', 'GW Open Source Program Office', 'Switch to the GW theme'],
             ['todo', 'todo', 'TODO Group', 'Switch to the TODO Group theme']].forEach(function (d) {
              var b = document.createElement('button');
              b.type = 'button';
              b.className = 'hdr-logo ' + d[0];
              b.setAttribute('data-theme', d[1]);
              b.setAttribute('aria-label', d[2] + '. ' + d[3]);
              b.title = d[3] + ' (or press t)';
              b.addEventListener('click', function (e) { e.stopPropagation(); setTheme(d[1]); b.blur(); });
              box.appendChild(b);
            });
            sec.appendChild(box);
          });
          function setTheme(name) {
            current = name;
            root.classList.toggle('theme-todo', name === 'todo');
            document.querySelectorAll('.hdr-logo').forEach(function (b) {
              b.classList.toggle('active', b.getAttribute('data-theme') === name);
            });
            try { localStorage.setItem('deck-theme', name); } catch (e) {}
            paintDarkBackgrounds();
          }
          // Dark slides get their background from a data attribute; point it at the theme color.
          function paintDarkBackgrounds() {
            if (!window.Reveal || !Reveal.getSlideBackground) return;
            sections.forEach(function (sec) {
              if (!sec.classList.contains('dark')) return;
              var bg = Reveal.getSlideBackground(sec);
              if (bg) bg.style.setProperty('background-color', 'var(--c-deep)', 'important');
            });
          }
          function start() {
            if (!window.Reveal) { setTimeout(start, 100); return; }
            Reveal.on('ready', function () { setTheme(current); });
            if (Reveal.isReady && Reveal.isReady()) setTheme(current);
            document.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
              if (e.key === 't' && !e.metaKey && !e.ctrlKey && !e.altKey) setTheme(current === 'gw' ? 'todo' : 'gw');
            });
          }
          start();
        });
        document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () {
          function load(slide) {
            if (!slide) return;
            slide.querySelectorAll('.embed-frame[data-embed-src]').forEach(function (el) {
              if (el.querySelector('iframe')) return;
              var f = document.createElement('iframe');
              f.src = el.getAttribute('data-embed-src');
              f.title = el.getAttribute('data-embed-title') || '';
              f.setAttribute('allowfullscreen', '');
              el.appendChild(f);
              // Sketch-style sites (p5.js) size their canvas to the window once at load,
              // so load them a second time after the slide has settled at its final size.
              if (el.hasAttribute('data-embed-reload')) {
                setTimeout(function () { f.src = el.getAttribute('data-embed-src'); }, 700);
              }
            });
          }
          function wire() {
            if (!window.Reveal) { setTimeout(wire, 100); return; }
            Reveal.on('ready', function (e) { load(e.currentSlide); });
            Reveal.on('slidechanged', function (e) { load(e.currentSlide); });
          }
          wire();
        });
        </script>
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false

## Skill, then review {.content-slide}

<div class="kicker">Part 1 · Design skill</div>

::: {.tiles}
::: {.tile}
[1 · Generate]{.tile-label}

Our internal OSPO Marketing & Comms team creates a flyer, newsletter, website, or other output.
:::
::: {.tile}
[2 · Review]{.tile-label}

The design skill checks the graphic against the brand and layout principles.
:::
::: {.tile}
[3 · Human decides]{.tile-label}

A person reads the report, fixes priorities, iterates, and approves.
:::
:::

::: notes
Repos: github.com/gw-ospo/gwospo-brand and github.com/gw-ospo/gw-design-review. The newest piece is the gw-presentation skill (github.com/gw-ospo/gw-presentation), which built this deck.
:::

## What the review checks {.content-slide}

<div class="kicker">Part 1 · Review process</div>

::: {.tiles .cols-4}
::: {.tile .slim}
[Proximity]{.tile-label}

Related things sit together.
:::
::: {.tile .slim}
[Alignment]{.tile-label}

Every element lines up with something.
:::
::: {.tile .slim}
[Repetition]{.tile-label}

One visual system, used consistently.
:::
::: {.tile .slim}
[Contrast]{.tile-label}

The main point is obvious.
:::
:::

::: notes
Plus brand rules: GW palette, accessible color pairings, approved fonts, and the OSCON extended palette. Output is a prioritized list of fixes.
:::

## How a review is written {.content-slide}

<div class="kicker">Part 1 · Review process</div>

<div class="report-slide">
<div class="report-steps">
<div><span class="chip chip-blue">Read</span><span><b>One-line read</b> and what the eye sees first, second, third.</span></div>
<div><span class="chip chip-good">Start here</span><span><b>What's working.</b> Two or three real strengths, before any criticism.</span></div>
<div><span class="chip chip-must">Must fix</span><span>Breaks a brand rule or accessibility. Not taste.</span></div>
<div><span class="chip chip-should">Should fix</span><span>Harder to read than it needs to be.</span></div>
<div><span class="chip chip-consider">Consider</span><span>A suggestion. Take it or leave it.</span></div>
<div><span class="chip chip-blue">Next</span><span><b>If you only do three things:</b> a short checklist.</span></div>
</div>
<div class="report-img"><img src="images/review-report.png" alt="The top of a design review written in markdown: the one-line read, reading order, what's working, and the first must-fix findings"></div>
</div>

::: notes
Show the markdown report (top of the real review of the awards flyer, 2026-09-11). Point out that it opens with what is working: the review is written for students and staff who made the piece themselves. Each finding names where the problem is, which rule it relates to, and the exact fix. Ends with "If you only do three things" and the checks that were run (palette audit, contrast). The reviewer does not redesign the work; it tells you what to change and why, then stops.
:::

## Review finding 1: an off-brand blue {.content-slide}

<div class="kicker">Part 1 · Review of the original</div>

<div class="flyer-slide">
<div class="flyer"><img src="images/awards-original.jpg" alt="Original GW OSPO 2026 Open Source Awards flyer"><span class="hl" style="left:0.00%;top:2.81%;width:100.00%;height:18.75%"><b>1</b></span><span class="hl" style="left:0.00%;top:81.56%;width:100.00%;height:14.06%"><b>2</b></span></div>
<div class="flyer-text">
<p class="lead-line">A flat blue that isn't in the GW palette runs through the page.</p>
<ul><li>Measured <b>#0096D5</b>, not Potomac <b>#0075C8</b></li><li>White text on it: <b>3.32:1</b>, large text only</li><li>On Potomac: <b>4.80:1</b>, passes at any size</li><li>Fix: swap both areas to Potomac</li></ul>
</div>
</div>

::: notes
Must fix #1. Highlight 1: stripe accents at the top. Highlight 2: the deadline banner. brand-checks C1 (no off-palette colour). Source: design review of the awards flyer, 2026-09-11.
:::

## Review finding 2: no Gazzetta {.content-slide}

<div class="kicker">Part 1 · Review of the original</div>

<div class="flyer-slide">
<div class="flyer"><img src="images/awards-original.jpg" alt="Original GW OSPO 2026 Open Source Awards flyer"><span class="hl" style="left:15.62%;top:24.69%;width:69.92%;height:6.88%"><b>1</b></span><span class="hl" style="left:5.86%;top:50.31%;width:46.48%;height:5.31%"><b>2</b></span><span class="hl" style="left:6.64%;top:67.19%;width:43.36%;height:3.75%"><b>3</b></span><span class="hl" style="left:55.47%;top:67.19%;width:40.23%;height:3.75%"><b>4</b></span><span class="hl" style="left:38.67%;top:84.38%;width:45.70%;height:9.69%"><b>5</b></span></div>
<div class="flyer-text">
<p class="lead-line">Every headline is set in a serif face. Gazzetta appears nowhere.</p>
<ul><li>Five headline moments, one serif face</li><li>Source Serif should stay rare: one word or a pull quote</li><li>Fix: reset all five in Gazzetta</li><li>No Gazzetta? Use Avenir Next Bold, not the serif</li></ul>
</div>
</div>

::: notes
Must fix #2. brand-checks T2 (Gazzetta carries headlines) and T5 (Source Serif stays rare). Highlights: title, prize amount, the two award headers, the deadline.
:::

## Review finding 3: hierarchy {.content-slide}

<div class="kicker">Part 1 · Review of the original</div>

<div class="flyer-slide">
<div class="flyer"><img src="images/awards-original.jpg" alt="Original GW OSPO 2026 Open Source Awards flyer"><span class="hl" style="left:14.84%;top:24.69%;width:71.88%;height:20.00%"><b>1</b></span><span class="hl" style="left:0.00%;top:48.12%;width:100.00%;height:15.62%"><b>2</b></span><span class="hl" style="left:0.00%;top:81.56%;width:100.00%;height:14.06%"><b>3</b></span></div>
<div class="flyer-text">
<p class="lead-line">The loudest shape is the prize amount. The deadline is last.</p>
<ul><li>Reading order: prize banner, photo, title, and only then the deadline</li><li>The hero block is centered; the rest is left-aligned</li><li>Fix: left-align the hero and give the deadline more weight</li><li>Or quiet the cream prize banner</li></ul>
</div>
</div>

::: notes
Should fix #3 (alignment) and #4 (contrast). Highlight 1: centered hero block. Highlight 2: cream prize banner, the highest-contrast shape. Highlight 3: the deadline banner, the actual call to action. The one job of this piece is to get students to apply by November 1.
:::

## Inside the design review repo {.content-slide}

<div class="kicker">Part 1 · The skill</div>

<div class="tiles tiles-4">
<div class="tile slim">
<span class="tile-label">SKILL.md</span>
The instructions Claude follows: how to look at a design and how to write the report.
</div>
<div class="tile slim">
<span class="tile-label">brand/</span>
<code>DESIGN.md</code> is the rulebook, <code>palette.json</code> the colors, <code>profile.md</code> who the reviews are for.
</div>
<div class="tile slim">
<span class="tile-label">references/</span>
<code>brand-checks.md</code>, <code>design-principles.md</code>, and <code>report-format.md</code>: what to check and how to write it.
</div>
<div class="tile slim">
<span class="tile-label">scripts/</span>
<code>contrast.py</code> and <code>palette_audit.py</code> measure; <code>rasterize.py</code> turns PDFs into images.
</div>
</div>

<p class="foot-note">Lives in <code>.claude/skills/gw-design-review/</code>. A ready-made <code>gw-design-review.zip</code> is included for claude.ai.</p>

::: notes
Repo: github.com/gw-ospo/gw-design-review. The skill follows the open Agent Skills format, so it is portable across tools; the only thing that differs is which folder each tool looks in. Brand rules live in one place (brand/DESIGN.md) so updating the rulebook updates the reviewer. The scripts give real measurements, so colors and contrast are checked, not guessed.
:::

## Using a skill with Claude {.content-slide}

<div class="kicker">Part 1 · The skill</div>

<div class="tiles tiles-3">
<div class="tile slim">
<span class="tile-label">claude.ai</span>
<ol>
<li>Download <code>gw-design-review.zip</code></li>
<li>Settings, then Capabilities, then Skills</li>
<li>Upload skill (don't unzip)</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="tile slim">
<span class="tile-label">Claude desktop, Cowork, Code</span>
<ol>
<li>Download the repo (Code, then Download ZIP)</li>
<li>Point Claude at the folder</li>
<li>Nothing to install</li>
</ol>
</div>
<div class="tile slim">
<span class="tile-label">Any other AI tool</span>
<ol>
<li>Attach the four text files</li>
<li>Ask for the report</li>
<li>No setup, no auto contrast checks</li>
</ol>
</div>
</div>

<p class="foot-note"><b>Then ask:</b> "Review this poster against our brand guidelines. It's a printed 11×17 for the OSCON call for papers."</p>

::: notes
Have three answers ready: what it is and where it will end up, who it is for and what they should do next, and whether it is OSCON or general OSPO (OSCON has three extra accent colors). Claude Code: git clone the repo, cd in, run claude; or symlink the skill into ~/.claude/skills to use it in any folder. Do not upload the GitHub repo zip to claude.ai; use the ready-made gw-design-review.zip. ChatGPT/Codex reads .agents/skills, so copy the folder there. Ask early, not at the end; it will not redesign your work; if it is wrong, say so and ask it to look again.
:::

## Three benefits with AI {.content-slide}

<div class="kicker">Part 2 · Quarto</div>

::: {.tiles}
::: {.tile}
[Modularity]{.tile-label}

Content and format live apart, so AI can edit one without breaking the other.
:::
::: {.tile}
[Efficiency]{.tile-label}

Plain text is short. Fewer characters means fewer tokens, lower cost, faster edits.
:::
::: {.tile}
[Correctness]{.tile-label}

Small readable files are easy for people to check and for Git to diff.
:::
:::

## Open Source Discovery & Curation {.content-slide}

<div class="kicker">Backup · Discovery</div>

::: {.tiles .cols-2}
::: {.tile .slim .compact}
[ORB · Open Source Repository Browser]{.tile-label}

- Built by the UC OSPO Network
- Maps and classifies open source projects across UC campuses
- Makes projects easier to find for researchers, students, and collaborators
- Raises visibility, recognition, and funding potential

[ORB on GitHub](https://github.com/UC-OSPO-Network/orb-showcase)
:::
::: {.tile .slim .compact}
[OSPO Radar · with Software Heritage]{.tile-label}

- Two-year, Sloan Foundation funded project
- Institutional portal and software assets dashboard for OSPOs
- Builds on CodeMeta metadata and Software Heritage archiving
- Includes an Open Science helpdesk and training

[OSPO-RADAR launch post](https://www.softwareheritage.org/2025/04/02/ospo-radar-project-launch/)
:::
:::

::: notes
ORB: github.com/UC-OSPO-Network/orb-showcase (UC Open Source Repository Browser Showcase). OSPO-RADAR = Open Source Program Office Research Assets Dashboard and Archival Resource. Source: softwareheritage.org/2025/04/02/ospo-radar-project-launch/. Software Heritage is collaborating with CURIOSS and seeking academic OSPOs to join. Add a screenshot of ORB or the Radar dashboard if one is available; the ORB demo site (orb-showcase-seven.vercel.app) returned 404 when checked.
:::
